loop_role: The self-evolve workspace: it builds the deterministic code graph, composes tier-fitted context envelopes, and drives gated apply-and-verify runs so the agent can improve its own codebase under evidence and budget constraints.

examples.title: Close the loop with EvolutionLoop re-analysis
examples.loop_role: Model evolve-01 as the loop-closing edge: after an apply run lands, `EvolutionLoop::run_once` re-scans `src/` via `GraphBuilder` and swaps in a fresh `Graph`, turning act back into perceive. Wire it as the transition edge from the apply/commit node to the graph node — no evolution step is complete until `LoopResult { reanalyzed, updated_nodes }` confirms the workspace model matches the new code.
examples.affects: Mutates the graph object everything else reads: node/edge sets, token counts per component, and therefore every downstream `ContextEnvelope.graph_revision`. Stale graph = stale evidence hashes, so the loop must treat `updated_nodes` as a revision bump that invalidates cached context envelopes and readiness reports.
examples.touch_ux: A circular-arrow rim around the graph node; when a re-analysis completes the whole canvas ripples once and every node badge recomputes. Tap shows `LoopResult` (`updated_nodes`, duration); long-press replays the last re-scan diff (nodes added/removed highlighted green/red). A stale-graph badge (amber dot) appears on any envelope node built from the old revision.

examples.title: Compose context tiers with ContextComposer
examples.loop_role: This is the perceive stage's throttle. `ContextComposer` owns which `ContextMode` (Map, Lite, Compact, Full, FullExtended, Custom, Preset) is active over the production `Graph` nodes; plan reads `included_nodes` and `estimate_tokens` before any model call. Wire it between the graph node and the envelope builder: graph → composer → envelope.
examples.affects: Directly sizes the context window object: `ContextModeSize` per tier, `ContextLayerSummary` per `NodeLayer`, and `ContextSummary` for the picker. Choosing `Custom` admits hand-picked nodes at skeleton detail; `Preset(name)` narrows to one preset. `TOKENS_PER_LINE` (10) is only a fallback for nodes without measured counts — canvas must mark estimated vs measured tokens differently.
examples.touch_ux: A vertical tier-slider node (Map at top, FullExtended at bottom) with a token-count badge per stop that fills/drains as you drag. Tap a tier to pin it; pinch on the slider expands to the per-layer breakdown (`ContextLayerSummary`); long-press a tier shows the exact node list it would include. The active tier glows; tiers exceeding the model window show red hatch marks.

examples.title: Ship hash-addressed ContextEnvelope bundles
examples.loop_role: The envelope is the perceive→plan handoff artifact: `build_envelope` projects the composer's included set at the active tier into `ProjectedDocument`s and seals them with a `content_hash`. Model the envelope as the object that travels on the edge into the model call — preview and outbound responses both carry the hash, and equality of hashes proves both sides describe the same bytes.
examples.affects: Binds context window contents to evidence integrity: `ContextEnvelope { mode, graph_revision, included, documents, total_tokens, content_hash }`. Non-Rust Code nodes ship verbatim in Lite/Custom (no skeleton exists) and are counted at full tokens — so envelope cost is honest, never optimistically projected. A changed hash means a changed context; the loop can cache, diff, and audit by hash.
examples.touch_ux: A sealed-envelope hexagon showing `total_tokens` and a truncated `content_hash` as its badge. Tap flips it open to the `ProjectedDocument` list (path, tokens each); pinch zooms from card view into a treemap of token share per document; long-press copies the hash and highlights every other canvas object stamped with the same hash (proving shared provenance). Hash mismatch vs current graph revision renders a broken-seal icon.

examples.title: Auto-fit tiers to the model window with TierMeasurer
examples.loop_role: Plugs into plan as the budget resolver: `RequestedMode::Auto` plus `fit_tier` walks the `TIER_LADDER` richest-first (FullExtended → Map) and picks the richest tier whose measured size fits `FitBudget::usable()`. Wire it upstream of the composer so the loop never proposes a context the model cannot hold.
examples.affects: Turns budget into a measured, not estimated, quantity: `FitBudget { context_length, output_reserve, fit_ratio }` with `output_reserve = max_tokens.min(context_length/4)`, and `TierMeasurer` really projects sources (strip comments / skeleton / map) to measure tier size — fixed fractions survive only as per-node fallbacks. `FitOutcome` records what fit and why; `io_reads` counts the disk cost of measuring.
examples.touch_ux: A gauge node shaped like a fuel dial: needle = `usable()` tokens, five tier notches on the dial. The auto-fit tier animates the needle settling on the richest fitting notch; tap shows `FitOutcome` (chosen tier, measured tokens, fallbacks used); a per-node fallback warning renders as a striped segment on the dial. Long-press pins a tier (switching `RequestedMode` from Auto to Fixed); pinch compares measured vs fallback estimates side by side.

examples.title: Navigate by ComponentCard map tier
examples.loop_role: The Map tier is the perceive stage for small windows: `build_map` emits one `ComponentCard` per component — doc line plus public symbol names — and `expand` pulls full detail on demand. Model it as a two-level loop: the model reads the resident map, decides what matters, then issues an expand retrieval; nothing is lost, detail is one call away.
examples.affects: Defines the resident-vs-retrieved split of the context window: `ContextMap.map_tokens` is the resident cost, `full_tokens` the cost it replaces. Each `ComponentCard` carries `tokens` and `lite_tokens` (what expanding full vs skeleton costs) and `more` for symbols beyond `MAX_SYMBOLS_PER_COMPONENT` — reported, not dropped, so the map never silently truncates.
examples.touch_ux: The map node is a grid of small cards; each card is a rounded chip with the component's doc line and a `tokens`/`lite_tokens` badge. Tap a card to expand it in place (skeleton view slides out — this is the `expand` call made visible); pinch out collapses back to the grid; long-press toggles between lite_tokens and full cost preview. Cards with `more > 0` show a '+N' corner ribbon.

examples.title: Stage and verify apply runs in shadow worktrees
examples.loop_role: This is the act stage with a built-in verify chute: `stage_run` spawns `selfware run --yolo` inside a shadow git worktree (never the live checkout), serialized through `APPLY_LOCK`; on exit `verify_staged_diff` checks the diff is non-empty, scoped to `src/` + `docs/`, and compiles (`cargo check`, 10-minute bound) before the run becomes `Staged`. Wire graph action → apply node → diagnostics/commit; nothing merges without the deliberate commit step.
examples.affects: Owns the trust state of changes: `ApplyStatus` (Running, Staged, Rejected(reason), Succeeded, Failed), typed `RejectReason`, and `StagedDiff { digest, files_changed, insertions, deletions, preview }`. `commit_staged` requires the exact digest and matching `base_revision` — a one-use token; replay yields `unknown_run` 404. Tests deliberately don't run here; compile is the authoritative minimum, deeper verification is CI's job — the canvas must show that honesty boundary.
examples.touch_ux: A conveyor-belt node: runs are tokens traveling left (Running, pulsing) to a staging pad (Staged, green seal) or a reject bin (Rejected, red, tap for the typed reason and capped stderr). The commit step is a physical two-finger drag of the staged token onto the live-branch node — the digest must match, shown as a key-fits-lock animation. Live badge: current run status + `files_changed`/`insertions`/`deletions` from `StagedDiff`. Long-press a rejected run opens the preserved shadow worktree for inspection.

examples.title: Gate actions through Gatekeeper compile and architecture checks
examples.loop_role: The verify stage's hard gate: `Gatekeeper::check_code_gates` evaluates compile/test and architecture constraints for an evolution action and returns a `GateResult`. Model it as a mandatory pass-through edge between act and remember — the loop may not record an outcome as success unless the gate passes.
examples.affects: Converts 'the model said it worked' into a typed `GateResult` the trust state can depend on. It is deliberately tiny (303 tokens) — a cheap, deterministic check that sits in front of every expensive model claim, matching the repo's stop-the-line rule: red gates stop the loop, they are never background noise.
examples.touch_ux: A portcullis/gate node on the act→remember edge: green when `GateResult` passes, red and physically blocking the edge when it fails — the connecting line visibly stops at the gate. Tap shows the gate checklist (compile, test, architecture) with per-item status; long-press reveals the exact failing command output. A gray gate means 'not yet run' — never render it green by default.

examples.title: Stream structured diagnostics from DiagnosticsEngine
examples.loop_role: Plugs into verify as the structured feedback channel: `DiagnosticsEngine::run` executes one of the fixed `AnalysisKind` commands (cargo_check, clippy, evolve tests) and parses JSON messages into `CompilerDiagnostic`s with `DiagnosticSpan`s, producing an `AnalysisReport`. The loop consumes this instead of raw build noise.
examples.affects: Shapes the tool-result object: browser requests can never supply executables or arbitrary args — the command set is fixed, output capped at `MAX_DIAGNOSTICS` (500) and `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` (64 KiB). Diagnostics carry real file/line spans, so verify feedback is evidence-addressable and can be cited by the grounded assistant rather than paraphrased.
examples.touch_ux: A radar-dish node that sweeps when an analysis runs; diagnostics land as pins on the affected file nodes (severity-colored: error red, warning amber). Tap a pin shows the `CompilerDiagnostic` message with its `DiagnosticSpan` highlighted in a peek-view of the source; pinch on the node toggles between the three `AnalysisKind` modes; the badge shows error/warning counts live. Long-press re-runs the same analysis kind.

examples.title: Evaluate merge readiness with honest GateState
examples.loop_role: The verify stage's scoreboard: `ReadinessEngine::evaluate` composes diagnostics, git status, and ontology validation into a `ReadinessReport` of `ReadinessGate`s, each with `GateEvidence` (source, detail, path, line). It also emits `DeterministicRecommendation`s — multi-hop `RecommendationHop` plans computed from the graph, not from model prose.
examples.affects: This is the trust/honesty backbone: `GateState` is Pass | Fail | Unknown, and Unknown is a first-class rendered state — a gate whose evidence wasn't collected must never show green. `evidence_complete: false` on a recommendation tells the UI the plan is partial. The `ready` flag is a conjunction of real gate states, so the loop's decision to merge is auditable per gate, per evidence line.
examples.touch_ux: A traffic-light cluster node, one lamp per `ReadinessGate` — green/amber/red map to Pass/Unknown/Fail, and Unknown is deliberately amber-blinking, never green. Tap a lamp lists its `GateEvidence` entries as tappable citation chips that jump to file:line; the recommendations panel shows each `DeterministicRecommendation` as a numbered hop chain you can drag onto the canvas as an action sequence. Badge: `ready` boolean plus count of non-Pass gates.

examples.title: Constrain model review with GroundedAssistant evidence
examples.loop_role: Plugs into plan as the model-facing review path with a grounding harness: `GroundedAssistant::review` requires claims and recommendations to cite `GroundingEvidence` IDs minted from exact workspace lines (`evidence_from_document`), and `validate_review_json` strips items with missing or unknown citations before they reach the UI; one malformed reply triggers `REVIEW_REPAIR_PROMPT` with full context retained.
examples.affects: Defines the evidence object and the trust state of model output: `GroundedClaim { text, evidence_ids }`, `GroundedRecommendation` with ordered `ActionHop`s, `TrustGateFinding`/`TrustGateSummary` from `gate_evidence_trust`, and `ReviewUsage` for token/cost accounting. The honesty rule is mechanical: uncited prose is deleted, not flagged — `trust_state: structural` means schema+citations were verified, never more.
examples.touch_ux: A magnifier-over-document node: each model claim renders as a speech chip physically tethered by lines to the evidence excerpts it cites; a claim with zero tethers is impossible to render (it was already stripped). Tap a tether jumps to the cited line range with `content_hash` shown; long-press a claim runs `gate_evidence_trust` and recolors the chip by trust finding. Badge: claims kept / claims stripped counts, plus `ReviewUsage.total_tokens` and cost.

examples.title: Scan context for injection with TrustReport
examples.loop_role: A trust boundary on the perceive edge: before any assembled context reaches the model, `analyze_source` tags it with a `SourceKind` (Workspace, ToolOutput, ModelOutput, External, Memory, User) and `TrustLevel`, and `scan_injection` hunts instruction_override, role_switch, hidden_unicode, exfiltration_hint, encoded_blob, and tool_directive patterns.
examples.affects: Adds a pollution dimension to every context object: `TrustReport { source_id, source_kind, ... }` with `InjectionFinding`s carrying kind, severity (high/medium/low), line, and excerpt. External and ToolOutput provenance demotes trust; a high-severity finding should block or quarantine the envelope, so the loop's context window is a defended boundary, not an open pipe.
examples.touch_ux: A shield-filter node sitting on the edge into the model call; content flows through it visibly and findings stick to the filter as splatter marks colored by severity. Tap a splatter shows the `InjectionFinding` excerpt and explanation; the source-kind tint (workspace = cool blue, external = hot orange) propagates to every downstream envelope chip so provenance is visible at a glance. Badge: highest severity seen + finding count; long-press quarantines the source.

examples.title: Select task-scoped files with ContextSelection
examples.loop_role: A smarter perceive stage: `select` takes a `TaskKind` (Extend, Refactor, Consolidate, Cleanup, Understand) and picks exactly the files the task needs — for Refactor, the target's source plus dependents (blast radius) plus dependencies (context); for Consolidate, files with duplicate functions from `FnDedupAnalyzer`; for Cleanup, files with reachability-dead code from `DeadCodeAnalyzer`.
examples.affects: Shrinks and focuses the context window object: `ContextSelection` is a ranked list of `SelectedFile`s, each annotated with the role it plays and why — so budget is spent on relevance, not tier brute force. Because selection is deterministic for the same target + graph revision, it composes cleanly with envelope hashing and caching.
examples.touch_ux: A spotlight node: type or pick a `TaskKind` and the canvas dims everything except the selected files, which light up role-tinted (target = white, dependents = amber 'do not break', dependencies = cool gray context). Tap a lit file shows its `SelectedFile` rationale; drag the spotlight to retarget; pinch widens/narrows the selection radius. Badge: selected file count + total selected tokens vs the Full tier cost it replaces.

examples.title: Reduce prompt size with reduce_source and dedup_context
examples.loop_role: The compression step inside perceive: `reduce_source` strips comments and `cfg(test)` blocks (`strip_cfg_test_blocks`) to produce the Compact tier, and `dedup_context` removes repeated content across assembled documents. Both the tier measurer and the envelope projector call these, so measured size and shipped size converge.
examples.affects: Directly trades fidelity for budget on the context window object: Compact is roughly 82% of full, Lite (skeletons) roughly 18%. The honest-accounting hook: what `TierMeasurer` measures is what `build_envelope` ships, because they share this exact machinery — the canvas should show reduction as a measured delta, not a marketing percentage.
examples.touch_ux: A compressor-press node: feed it a document and it visibly squeezes — comments and test blocks flake off as gray particles with a live token counter dropping. Tap toggles before/after diff view (stripped ranges shown as folded gutters); pinch adjusts between strip-comments-only and strip-cfg-test levels; the badge shows tokens before → after and the realized ratio. Long-press previews what the same reduction costs in lost evidence lines.

examples.title: Launch self-improvement directions from Preset menu
examples.loop_role: The plan stage's menu: each `Preset` (e.g. `symbol-context-selection`, `dedup-clutter-strip`) bundles a task prompt, the logical-layer capability it touches, the invariants the run must not break, a `context_recipe`, and a `verify` command. `render_prompt` assembles it for the model. Wire preset → context recipe (composer) → apply run → verify — a full loop in one tap.
examples.affects: Parameterizes the whole loop per run: invariants become refuse-conditions on the trust state ('Cited evidence stays line-accurate', 'Selection is deterministic'), `verify` (default: `cargo build && cargo test; no clippy regressions`) becomes the gate, and the context recipe sets the envelope contents. Presets turn open-ended self-modification into enumerated, guard-railed directions.
examples.touch_ux: A menu-carousel node of preset tiles, each showing title, direction color (context = teal, refactor = violet, safety = red), and its capability tag. Tap a tile expands it to show task, invariants, and verify; a two-finger swipe right launches it as an apply run (spawning the evolve-06 conveyor). Invariant chips are draggable onto gates to attach them as refuse-conditions. Badge: number of presets + which direction is currently running.

examples.title: Propose actions, mutate only through GitEngine
examples.loop_role: Separates proposal from mutation in the act stage: `ActionEngine::propose` builds non-mutating `Action` proposals (Extend, Connect, BlockEvolution, Notify) and returns an `ActionResult` with only a suggested `branch_name` — the actual guarded branch creation is owned by `GitEngine::create_branch`, which first reports `GitStatusReport` / `GitFileState`. Model them as two nodes: propose (free, safe) → commit-to-git (guarded, explicit).
examples.affects: Keeps the loop's mutation surface honest: the stateless `ActionEngine` cannot touch the working tree by construction; `BranchResult` records what git actually did. Clean-tree checks at the apply endpoint guarantee a staged diff is exactly the agent's work — provenance of every change on the loop is attributable.
examples.touch_ux: Two linked nodes: a thought-bubble (proposals) and a locked padlock (git). Bubbles float freely — tap to preview the suggested branch name; dragging a bubble onto the padlock triggers `GitEngine::status` first, showing dirty files as warning chips that block the drop until resolved. A successful `create_branch` animates a new branch line growing off the repo node. Badge on the padlock: clean/dirty tree state and current branch.

examples.title: Version the graph with OntologyEvolver stability gates
examples.loop_role: The remember stage: `OntologyStore::save`/`load` persists the evolve graph to YAML and `validate_graph` catches `DanglingEdge`s in a `ValidationReport`; `OntologyEvolver::propose_change` turns an `OntologyProposal` (AddConcept, MergeConcepts, SplitConcept) into an `OntologyVersion` of explicit `OntologyOperation`s (AddNode, RemoveNode, AddEdge, RemoveEdge) that `apply_change` commits through stability gates.
examples.affects: Gives the loop durable, auditable memory: graph revisions are versioned operations, not silent mutations — every concept add/merge/split is a replayable `OntologyVersion`. Validation failures (dangling edges) feed the readiness gates, so corrupt memory blocks the loop instead of poisoning downstream context.
examples.touch_ux: A version-tree node: each persisted graph is a ring on a timeline; tap a ring to diff it against the current graph (added/removed nodes and edges animate). Proposing a change shows the `OntologyOperation` list as a checklist you approve item-by-item before `apply_change` commits. `DanglingEdge`s render as red broken threads hanging off nodes — tap to see the `ValidationReport`. Badge: current version id + validation pass/fail.

examples.title: Answer queries with GroundedFact citations
examples.loop_role: A perceive-side Q&A path: `GraphRag::query` answers natural-language questions with `GroundedFact`s — each fact carries `file`, `line_range`, an exact unnumbered `excerpt`, and a SHA-256 `content_hash` of the complete file bytes, giving a stable, verifiable identity for every citation.
examples.affects: Upgrades model-facing answers into evidence objects: a fact's `content_hash` lets the loop detect when the underlying file drifted since the fact was minted (hash mismatch = stale citation). This is the same honesty machinery as the envelope — citations are bytes-plus-range, not vibes — and it feeds claims in the grounded assistant and readiness evidence alike.
examples.touch_ux: A question-mark satellite orbiting the graph: ask by tapping and typing; answers arrive as fact chips pinned by threads to the exact file:line ranges, each chip showing its truncated `content_hash`. A stale fact (file changed) fades and shows a 'hash drifted' badge — tap to re-mint. Pinch on a chip expands the excerpt to full surrounding context. Badge: facts on screen + count of drifted citations.

examples.title: Hunt dead and duplicate code to feed act
examples.loop_role: Analysis that feeds the plan stage with targets: `DeadCodeAnalyzer::find` does reachability-based dead-code detection producing `DeadSymbol`s; `DeduplicationAnalyzer::find_duplicates` finds exact and near-duplicate clusters via `jaccard` similarity (`DuplicateKind`, `DuplicatePair`); `FnDedupAnalyzer::find` works at function level with `FnLocation`s and `DuplicateFnPair`s. Wire their outputs into `context_selector` (Consolidate/Cleanup task kinds) and into preset runs.
examples.affects: Creates the work items on the loop: each `DeadSymbol` or `DuplicateFnPair` is a candidate act target with real file/line locations, and removing them shrinks future context windows (less code = cheaper envelopes). Because detection is deterministic and reachability- or similarity-based, findings are evidence the readiness path can cite, not model speculation.
examples.touch_ux: A pair of detector nodes: a skull icon (dead code) and a twins icon (dupes). Findings render as grayed-out symbols (dead) or glowing link-lines between duplicate functions with a Jaccard score label; tap a link shows the pair side-by-side with the similarity computation; long-press sends the finding to the context selector as a Consolidate/Cleanup task. Badges: dead symbol count, duplicate cluster count, and tokens reclaimable.

examples.title: Preview deletions before touching source
examples.loop_role: A pre-act simulation step: `preview_deletion` takes a `DeletionTarget` and returns a `DeletionPreview` — the `ImpactEdge`s that would break and the `VerificationStep`s to run afterward — without mutating anything; `require_executable` keeps the preview honest about what verification can actually run. Model it as a sandbox branch off the act node: simulate first, then decide.
examples.affects: Adds a blast-radius object to the loop: `ImpactEdge`s name the dependents that would break, giving the plan stage a concrete cost for each deletion candidate (composing with dead-code findings from evolve-18). The preview is non-mutating by construction, so exploring destructive actions costs nothing and leaves no trust-state residue.
examples.touch_ux: A ghost-scissors node: hover-drag it over a symbol and the canvas renders the deletion as a ghost preview — the symbol turns translucent, `ImpactEdge`s light up as red fracture lines to dependents, and a `VerificationStep` checklist slides in at the bottom. Release to discard; a deliberate two-finger hold converts the preview into a real action proposal. Tap a fracture line to see exactly which dependent breaks. Badge: impacted edge count.

examples.title: Host the whole loop on EvolveServer
examples.loop_role: The stage everything runs on: `EvolveServer` (axum) wires the graph, `ContextComposer`, `ActionEngine`, `IdeEngine`, `DiagnosticsEngine`, `GitEngine`, `ReadinessEngine`, and `GroundedAssistant` behind one HTTP router with a session-token header (`x-selfware-session`) and a strict CSP. `start`/`start_with_shutdown` run the workspace; `graph_json`/`save_graph` expose the loop state; `apply_registry` tracks runs. Every other node in this file is a route on this server.
examples.affects: Owns the shared loop objects as `Arc<RwLock<…>>` state: the graph revision, the composer mode, the apply registry — so concurrent canvas interactions are serialized through real locks, and `FitBudget`'s output-reserve convention (`max_tokens.min(context_length/4)`) is defined here and reused by context_fit. Session token + CSP make the loop's UI surface a defended boundary, matching the context_trust story.
examples.touch_ux: The canvas itself: the server is the floor plate under all other nodes, its health shown as a subtle grid tint (green grid = session valid, gray = expired token). Pinch fully out to see the whole loop as one routed system with live request edges pulsing between nodes; tap the floor shows server meta (routes, session, active apply runs). Long-press triggers graceful shutdown via `start_with_shutdown`. Badge: active session indicator + count of in-flight requests.
